questions.title: Question 1: A stack by hand (Lecture 15, Exercise 1) (12 marks)
questions.prompt: Perform these operations on an empty stack: `push(14)`, `push(39)`, `push(26)`, `pop()`, `push(28)`, `push(17)`, `pop()`, `pop()`, `push(87)`, `pop()`. (a) Show the stack after each operation. (b) What is the sequence of values popped? (c) How many elements are left? (d) Which item is popped next? (12 marks)

steps.title: The stack after each operation
steps.body: 14; 14, 39; 14, 39, 26; pop gives 26 and leaves 14, 39; 14, 39, 28; 14, 39, 28, 17; pop gives 17; pop gives 28 and leaves 14, 39; 14, 39, 87; pop gives 87 and leaves 14, 39. (6 marks)

steps.title: The popped sequence
steps.body: 26, 17, 28, 87. Only consecutive pops come out in reverse order of the pushes. (2 marks)

steps.title: Elements left
steps.body: Two: 14 and 39. (2 marks)

steps.title: The next pop
steps.body: 39, the top of the remaining stack. (2 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Popped: 26, 17, 28, 87. Two elements are left (14, 39) and 39 is popped next.

questions.title: Question 2: A queue by hand (Lecture 16, Exercise 1) (12 marks)
questions.prompt: Perform these operations on an empty queue: `enqueue(52)`, `enqueue(96)`, `enqueue(63)`, `dequeue()`, `enqueue(28)`, `enqueue(86)`, `dequeue()`, `enqueue(69)`, `dequeue()`. (a) Show the queue after each operation. (b) What is the sequence of dequeued values? (c) What is the length of the queue at the end? (d) Which item is in front and which is at the tail? (12 marks)

steps.title: The queue after each operation
steps.body: 52; 52, 96; 52, 96, 63; dequeue gives 52 and leaves 96, 63; 96, 63, 28; 96, 63, 28, 86; dequeue gives 96 and leaves 63, 28, 86; 63, 28, 86, 69; dequeue gives 63 and leaves 28, 86, 69. (6 marks)

steps.title: The dequeued sequence
steps.body: 52, 96, 63: the order of the first three enqueues. (2 marks)

steps.title: The length
steps.body: Three elements: 28, 86, 69. (2 marks)

steps.title: Front and tail
steps.body: The front is 28 and the tail is 69. (2 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Dequeued: 52, 96, 63. The queue holds 28, 86, 69 (length 3), with 28 in front and 69 at the tail.

questions.title: Question 3: The array stack (14 marks)
questions.prompt: Implement an array stack of `Integer` values with the methods `Stack1(int n)`, `isEmpty`, `size`, `isFull`, `push`, `peek` and `pop`. The constructor sets `top` to -1. State the value of `top` when the stack is empty, has one element, is full, and overflows. (14 marks)

steps.title: The fields and the constructor
steps.body: `private Integer[] stack; private int top;` and `public Stack1(int n) { stack = new Integer[n]; top = -1; }`. (3 marks)

steps.title: The tests
steps.body: `isEmpty` is `top == -1`; `size` is `top + 1`; `isFull` is `top == stack.length - 1`. (3 marks)

steps.title: push, peek and pop
steps.body: `push`: if `isFull()` print "Stack Overflow! Can not insert..." and return `false`, otherwise `stack[++top] = num` and return `true`. `peek`: return `stack[top]` if the stack is not empty, otherwise `null`. `pop`: if not empty return `stack[top--]`, otherwise print "Stack Underflow! Nothing to remove" and return `null`. (5 marks)

steps.title: The values of top
steps.body: Empty: -1. One element: 0. Full (N elements): N - 1. Overflow: N. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Check.** For a capacity of 5, five pushes give `top` = 4 and `isFull()` is `true`; a sixth push prints the overflow message and changes nothing.

questions.title: Question 4: Memory diagrams of the linked structures (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) A linked stack is empty. Draw the memory after `push("CSI247")`, `push("CSI243")`, `push("CSI141")` and `pop()`. (b) A linked queue is empty. Draw the memory after `enqueue("19")`, `enqueue("28")` and `dequeue()`. In each, give the addresses you use and say which node is garbage. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a): the pushes
steps.body: The stack object holds `top`. `push("CSI247")`: a node at 100 with next `null`; `top` = 100. `push("CSI243")`: a node at 200 with next 100; `top` = 200. `push("CSI141")`: a node at 300 with next 200; `top` = 300. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (a): the pop
steps.body: `pop()` saves "CSI141" and sets `top = top.next`, so `top` = 200 (300 crossed out). Nothing refers to the node at 300, so it is garbage. The stack is CSI243 above CSI247. (2 marks)

steps.title: Part (b): the enqueues
steps.body: The queue object holds `front` and `tail`. `enqueue("19")` on the empty queue: a node at 100; `front` = `tail` = 100. `enqueue("28")`: a node at 200; the 100 node's next = 200; `tail` = 200; `front` stays 100. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b): the dequeue
steps.body: `dequeue()` saves "19" and sets `front = front.next`, so `front` = 200 and `tail` = 200. The node at 100 is isolated: garbage. (2 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** (a) `top` = 200, node 300 is garbage. (b) `front` = `tail` = 200, node 100 is garbage.

questions.title: Question 5: The array queue (12 marks)
questions.prompt: An array queue has capacity 4, with `front` and `tail` both -1 when empty. (a) After `enqueue("A")`, `enqueue("B")`, `enqueue("C")`, `enqueue("D")` and `dequeue()`, state `front`, `tail` and `size()`. (b) What happens when `enqueue("E")` is then called with the lecture's `isFull()`? (c) Give a repair. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: After the four enqueues `front` is 0 and `tail` is 3. The dequeue returns "A" and moves `front` to 1. `size()` is `tail - front + 1 = 3`. The array still holds A, B, C, D. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `isFull()` compares the size (3) with the length (4), so it is `false` and the enqueue goes ahead. `tail++` makes `tail` 4 and `queue[4]` is outside the array: `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Slot 0 is free, but `tail` only moves forwards. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: Refuse the enqueue when `tail == queue.length - 1` (no room after the tail), or use a circular queue, in which the last element is connected to the first so that the freed slots are reused. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** `front` 1, `tail` 3, size 3; the next enqueue throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`; test for room after the tail.

questions.title: Question 6: Types of queue and applications (10 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) Name and describe the four types of queue in the lecture. (b) Choose a stack, a queue or a priority queue for: undo in a text editor; students in a cafeteria; the processes of a multitasking operating system; the Back button of a web browser. (10 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: A normal queue is FIFO. A circular queue has its last element connected to the first, forming a circle. A double-ended queue (deque) allows insertions and deletions at both the front and the tail. A priority queue orders items by key value, with the lowest (or highest) key always in front, and insertions keep the ordering. (6 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: Undo: a stack (the latest change is undone first). Cafeteria: a queue (first come, first served). Operating system processes: a priority queue (the process with the lowest or highest key is at the front). Back button: a stack (the last page visited is returned to first). (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Rule.** Newest first: stack. Oldest first: queue. Most important first: priority queue.
